selected_hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Mercado de San Juan Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore one of Mexico City's most beloved gourmet markets in the heart of the city center. Sample exotic cheeses, fresh seafood tostadas, traditional tamales, and artisanal mezcal. This market is a favorite among locals and chefs alike, offering an authentic taste of Mexican culinary diversity without tourist markup. Ideal for Day 1 arrival since it's walkable from central hotels and open until evening.

experiences.name: Frida Kahlo Museum (La Casa Azul)
experiences.description: Visit the iconic Blue House where Frida Kahlo was born and lived. Explore her personal belongings, artwork, and the vibrant colonial architecture that defined her life. Book tickets in advance online to avoid long queues. The surrounding Coyoacán neighborhood is charming, walkable, and filled with cafes and artisan markets perfect for an afternoon stroll after the museum.

experiences.name: Coyoacán Neighborhood & Local Market Walk
experiences.description: Wander through the bohemian streets of Coyoacán, one of Mexico City's most culturally rich and walkable neighborhoods. Visit the Mercado de Coyoacán for traditional street food including tostadas, enchiladas, and fresh aguas frescas. Browse artisan stalls, watch street performers in the main plaza, and soak in the colonial atmosphere. Pair this with the Frida Kahlo Museum visit on the same day to maximize location efficiency.

experiences.name: Tacos & Street Food Evening in Roma Norte
experiences.description: Join a guided evening street food walk through Roma Norte, one of Mexico City's trendiest yet authentically local neighborhoods. Taste al pastor tacos from legendary taquerias, try elotes (grilled corn), churros, and traditional atole drinks. The neighborhood is safe, vibrant at night, and centrally located, making it perfect for an early evening activity that doesn't require long travel after a day of sightseeing.

experiences.name: Templo Mayor Archaeological Site & Museum
experiences.description: Discover the ancient Aztec ceremonial center at the heart of Mexico City, built on the ruins of Tenochtitlán. The on-site museum houses thousands of artifacts including stone sculptures, ceremonial offerings, and detailed exhibits explaining Aztec cosmology and daily life. Located steps from the Zócalo in the historic center, this experience is easily combined with other Centro Histórico activities, minimizing travel time and maximizing cultural immersion.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Mexico City
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take the Metro Line 5 from Terminal Aérea station to get to Centro Histórico affordably (around 5 MXN). Check in to your boutique stay and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world — completely free. Admire the Metropolitan Cathedral and the National Palace exterior. Pop into the National Palace to see Diego Rivera's famous murals at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along Madero Street, a pedestrian avenue lined with historic buildings and street performers. Explore the nearby Templo Mayor archaeological zone from the outside (visit inside another day). Settle into the neighborhood vibe.

meals.breakfast: Skip or grab a quick snack at the airport before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a late lunch / early dinner at a local taquería near the Zócalo — try tacos de canasta or tacos al pastor for 15–25 MXN each. Look for busy street stalls on República de Uruguay street.
meals.dinner: Visit Mercado de San Juan (about 10 min walk) for an affordable and authentic dinner. Try a comida corrida (set menu) at one of the market fondas for around 80–120 MXN including soup, main, and drink.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 starts post-arrival. Metro is the cheapest and fastest way from the airport. Keep small change handy for street food and Metro fares. Store valuables securely upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Templo Mayor Museum (entrance ~90 MXN, free on Sundays). Explore the ancient Aztec ruins right in the heart of the city. Spend 1.5–2 hours walking through the excavation site and museum exhibits.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire the stunning Art Nouveau exterior and peek into the lobby for free. Then walk to Alameda Central park for a relaxing afternoon among locals. Visit the nearby Museo Mural Diego Rivera (entrance ~50 MXN) to see the iconic 'Sueño de una Tarde Dominical' mural.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) on Calle Dolores for a unique cultural experience. Then head back toward the Zócalo area for evening people-watching and street entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local market breakfast stall — try chilaquiles or tamales with atole at Mercado Abelardo Rodríguez for around 50–70 MXN.
meals.lunch: Comida corrida at a no-frills restaurant near Alameda Central — full three-course set lunch for 80–100 MXN. Look for handwritten menus on chalkboards outside.
meals.dinner: Street tacos and quesadillas near the Zócalo evening market stalls — budget 60–80 MXN for a satisfying meal. Try quesadillas with huitlacoche or flor de calabaza.

day_by_day.notes: Bellas Artes is free to enter the ground floor. Sundays offer free museum entry across many national museums — plan accordingly. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro to Coyoacán neighborhood (Line 3 to Viveros station, ~5 MXN). Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum 'La Casa Azul' — book tickets online in advance (~270 MXN). Explore the colorful cobblestone streets around the museum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Coyoacán's central market (Mercado de Coyoacán) for local crafts and snacks. Visit the nearby Jardín Centenario and Plaza Hidalgo, the lively main square. Explore the free outdoor murals and colonial architecture throughout the neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico via Metro. Visit the rooftop terrace bar at Gran Hotel Ciudad de México for a drink with a stunning Zócalo view — budget one drink (~100–150 MXN) for the experience. Walk the illuminated streets of the historic center at night.

meals.breakfast: Grab fresh-baked pastries (pan dulce) and café de olla from a local panadería near your hotel — around 30–40 MXN.
meals.lunch: Eat at Mercado de Coyoacán — try tostadas de tinga or enchiladas at one of the market stalls for 60–90 MXN. The market is famous for its affordable, delicious local food.
meals.dinner: Back in Centro, try a pozole or menudo at a traditional cantina — look for places on Calle Uruguay or around Mercado de San Juan for 80–120 MXN.

day_by_day.notes: Frida Kahlo Museum sells out fast — book online at least a few days ahead. Coyoacán is best explored on foot. The neighborhood is very safe and lively during the day.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early Metro to Teotihuacán archaeological zone (catch a bus from Terminal Central del Norte — Metro Line 5 to Autobuses del Norte, then a 45-min bus for ~50 MXN each way). Arrive early to beat crowds. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun and Pyramid of the Moon (entrance ~90 MXN).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Avenue of the Dead and the Temple of Quetzalcoatl at Teotihuacán. Browse local artisan stalls outside the site for affordable souvenirs. Head back to Mexico City by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and recover near your hotel. Walk along the pedestrian streets of Centro Histórico and browse street vendors. Enjoy the vibrant nighttime atmosphere around the Zócalo.

meals.breakfast: Pack a light breakfast from a nearby panadería or OXXO convenience store before heading out early — around 30–50 MXN.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the small restaurants just outside the Teotihuacán entrance — try barbacoa or gorditas for 80–120 MXN. Avoid the overpriced restaurants right at the main gate.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a sit-down meal at a local fondita in Centro Histórico — try mole negro with rice and beans for 100–150 MXN. You've earned it after a big day!

day_by_day.notes: Start very early (7:00–8:00 AM) to avoid heat and crowds at Teotihuacán. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water — it gets hot. The round trip from Centro takes about 1.5–2 hours total travel time.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Mercado de la Merced, one of the largest and most authentic traditional markets in Mexico City — free to enter. Explore the stalls selling spices, chiles, herbs, and local produce. A true sensory cultural experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the free Museo de la Ciudad de México (City Museum) on Pino Suárez street to learn about the city's history. Walk to the nearby Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles), a stunning 18th-century building — browse the interior Sanborns café for free. Revisit any favorite spots in Centro Histórico for last-minute photos.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening stroll around the Zócalo and Madero Street. Pick up last-minute souvenirs from street vendors (bargain respectfully). Enjoy a farewell meal in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Have a proper Mexican breakfast at Mercado de la Merced — try huevos rancheros or enfrijoladas with fresh juice for 60–80 MXN.
meals.lunch: Try a torta (Mexican sandwich) from a popular torta stand in Centro — tortas de milanesa or pierna for 40–60 MXN. Pair with an agua fresca from a street vendor.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a traditional pulquería or cantina — enjoy pulque (traditional fermented drink) and botanas (free bar snacks) for a truly local experience. Budget 100–150 MXN for drinks and snacks.

day_by_day.notes: La Merced market is best visited in the morning when it's most active. Keep an eye on your belongings in busy market areas. Save Metro fare receipts — you can reuse cards for return trips. Enjoy your last evening soaking up the incredible energy of Mexico City!

trip_options.title: Classic Mexico City Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer from airport to boutique hotel in Centro Histórico (approximately 45–60 min by taxi or Uber, ~$15–20 USD). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely walk around the Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest public squares in the world. Explore the exterior of the Metropolitan Cathedral and admire the Palacio Nacional facade. Stroll down Calle Madero, a vibrant pedestrian street lined with historic architecture, street performers, and local vendors.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Templo Mayor archaeological site area for a golden-hour atmosphere, then enjoy your first proper Mexico City dinner nearby. Explore the side streets of Centro Histórico as the city lights up at night.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — in-flight or airport meal before landing.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick and authentic bite near the hotel at Mercado de San Juan or a nearby taqueria — try tacos de canasta or tortas (~$5–8 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at El Cardenal (Centro Histórico location) — a beloved mid-range institution serving traditional Mexican cuisine like chiles en nogada and mole. Budget ~$20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light given the afternoon arrival. Comfortable walking shoes are essential. Exchange some currency or use ATMs in the hotel area for convenience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Templo Mayor Museum (open from 9:00 AM) — an extraordinary archaeological site right in the heart of Centro Histórico, built on the ruins of the Aztec capital Tenochtitlán. Allow 1.5–2 hours. Entry ~$5 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the Palacio de Bellas Artes to admire its stunning Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture. Visit the murals inside by Diego Rivera and other Mexican masters (entry to ground floor is free; upper galleries ~$3 USD). Afterward, explore the nearby Alameda Central park for a relaxing stroll among locals.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the bohemian neighborhood of Barrio Chino (Chinatown) or head to the lively streets around República de Uruguay for street food exploration. End the evening with a mezcal tasting at a local mezcalería.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try chilaquiles or tamales at a local fondita (~$5–8 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de San Juan — a gourmet market with stalls offering everything from fresh seafood tostadas to artisan cheeses and exotic fruits (~$8–12 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Azul Histórico, a beautiful restaurant set in a colonial courtyard serving refined Mexican regional cuisine. Budget ~$20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays — if Day 2 falls on a Monday, swap with the Palacio de Bellas Artes morning visit. Carry a light jacket as March mornings can be cool.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Teotihuacán — take an early bus from Terminal Norte (about 1 hour, ~$3 USD each way) to explore the ancient pyramids of the Sun and Moon. Climb the Pyramid of the Sun for panoramic views and walk the Avenue of the Dead. Arrive early (site opens at 9:00 AM) to beat crowds and heat. Entry ~$5 USD.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mexico City by early afternoon. Stop by the neighborhood of Tlatelolco on the way back to see the Plaza de las Tres Culturas — a powerful site where Aztec ruins, a colonial church, and modern architecture coexist.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in Centro Histórico and explore the street food scene around Plaza Garibaldi, where mariachi bands perform nightly. Try street snacks like elotes (corn) and churros.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab a torta or tamale from a street vendor near the bus terminal (~$3–5 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Teotihuacán — eat at one of the on-site restaurants like La Gruta, a restaurant set inside an actual cave/grotto. Budget ~$15–20 USD per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner near Plaza Garibaldi — try pozole or birria at a traditional cantina like Salón Corona or a local fondita (~$10–15 USD per person).

day_by_day.notes: Wear sunscreen and bring water for Teotihuacán — the site is very exposed. Start as early as possible (ideally by 8:30 AM at the bus terminal). Comfortable, sturdy shoes are a must.

day_by_day.morning: Take the Metro (Line 3, ~$0.30 USD) south to the Coyoacán neighborhood. Visit the Frida Kahlo Museum (Casa Azul) — book tickets in advance online as they sell out quickly (~$12 USD). Explore the iconic blue house and her personal belongings, art, and life story.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Coyoacán's charming streets and central market (Mercado de Coyoacán) — a colorful local market perfect for trying antojitos and picking up handmade souvenirs. Visit the nearby Diego Rivera Anahuacalli Museum if time allows (~$5 USD).
day_by_day.evening: Head back toward Centro or explore the nearby Colonia Roma neighborhood (a short Uber ride) for its trendy café and restaurant scene, tree-lined streets, and Art Deco architecture.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast in Coyoacán at a local café near the main square — try pan dulce with café de olla (~$5–7 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch at Mercado de Coyoacán — tostadas de tinga or enfrijoladas from one of the market stalls (~$6–10 USD).
meals.dinner: Dinner in Colonia Roma at Contramar (seafood) or Maximo Bistrot — both are beloved mid-range spots with excellent local and seasonal menus. Budget ~$20–30 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Frida Kahlo Museum tickets at least 1–2 weeks in advance at museofridakahlo.org.mx. Coyoacán is best explored on foot — it's a very walkable, safe neighborhood popular with families and artists.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología (National Museum of Anthropology) in Chapultepec — one of the greatest museums in the world, housing the Aztec Sun Stone and priceless pre-Hispanic artifacts. Allow at least 2–3 hours. Entry ~$5 USD. Located inside Bosque de Chapultepec, Latin America's largest urban park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Chapultepec Park, visit the Chapultepec Castle (Castillo de Chapultepec) for sweeping city views and Mexican history exhibits (~$4 USD entry). Afterward, explore the upscale Polanco neighborhood nearby — window shop on Presidente Masaryk Avenue and enjoy the cosmopolitan atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Centro Histórico for a final evening. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at artisan shops on Calle Moneda or near the Zócalo. Enjoy a farewell dinner with a view.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café in Centro — huevos rancheros or molletes (~$6–9 USD).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Polanco at a casual spot — try tacos at El Turix (famous cochinita pibil tacos, ~$5–8 USD) or a café terrace lunch.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at La Opera Bar — a historic cantina in Centro Histórico open since 1876, with a bullet hole in the ceiling allegedly made by Pancho Villa. Great atmosphere, traditional Mexican food, and cocktails. Budget ~$20–28 USD per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Anthropology Museum is closed on Mondays — plan accordingly. Chapultepec Park is very popular on weekends with families. Keep valuables secure in crowded areas. Check flight departure time for Day 6 to plan final morning accordingly.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Mexico City Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Centro Histórico, Mexico City Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Mexico City International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer from the airport to your boutique hotel in Centro Histórico. Check-in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity at the hotel.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk through the iconic Zócalo (Plaza de la Constitución), one of the largest city squares in the world. Explore the exterior of the Metropolitan Cathedral and admire the Palacio Nacional facade. Stroll along Madero Street, a vibrant pedestrian boulevard lined with colonial architecture, boutiques, and the stunning Casa de los Azulejos (House of Tiles).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the rooftop terrace of a nearby boutique bar overlooking the historic center skyline. Dinner at Azul Histórico, a celebrated restaurant set in a colonial courtyard inside the Centro Cultural de España, specializing in refined traditional Mexican cuisine with an emphasis on regional ingredients and heirloom recipes.

meals.lunch: Light welcome snack or room service at the hotel upon check-in — charcuterie board, fresh fruit, and artisanal agua fresca
meals.dinner: Azul Histórico — signature dishes such as mole negro with duck confit, chiles en nogada (seasonal), and house-made tortillas; pair with a premium mezcal flight

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance through the hotel concierge. Carry comfortable walking shoes for the cobblestone streets of Centro Histórico. March weather in Mexico City is typically warm and dry (low-to-mid 20s°C), ideal for evening strolls.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Templo Mayor archaeological site and its world-class on-site museum. Discover the ruins of the Aztec empire's most sacred temple at the heart of ancient Tenochtitlán. A knowledgeable expert guide will provide deep cultural and historical context, including the significance of the dual shrines dedicated to Huitzilopochtli and Tlaloc.
day_by_day.afternoon: Exclusive guided visit to the Palacio Nacional to see Diego Rivera's monumental murals depicting the entire history of Mexico — a breathtaking artistic and cultural masterpiece. Afterward, a curated walk through the artisan market Mercado de Artesanías La Ciudadela, where you can browse and purchase high-quality Mexican crafts, textiles, and ceramics from across the country.
day_by_day.evening: Cocktail hour at Bar La Opera, one of Mexico City's most legendary and atmospheric bars dating back to 1876, complete with ornate Belle Époque interiors and a famous bullet hole in the ceiling attributed to Pancho Villa. Dinner at Pujol, ranked among the world's top restaurants, offering Chef Enrique Olvera's iconic tasting menu that reimagines Mexican culinary tradition through avant-garde techniques — book well in advance.

meals.breakfast: In-hotel breakfast at the boutique hotel — freshly baked pan dulce, chilaquiles verdes, tropical fruit platter, and specialty Mexican coffee
meals.lunch: Café El Popular or El Cardenal near the Zócalo — traditional Mexican comida corrida featuring sopa de lima, arroz con leche, and handmade tortillas in an authentic setting beloved by locals
meals.dinner: Pujol — multi-course tasting menu featuring the legendary Mole Madre (aged mole sauce), baby corn with coffee mayonnaise, and innovative seasonal dishes; premium wine and mezcal pairing available

day_by_day.notes: Reservations at Pujol are essential and should be secured weeks in advance — the hotel concierge can assist. The Templo Mayor is closed on Mondays; confirm opening hours. Wear layers as temperatures can drop in the evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Private chauffeured excursion to Teotihuacán (approximately 50 km northeast of the city, about 1 hour by car). Explore the magnificent pre-Columbian city with a private archaeologist guide — climb the Pyramid of the Sun and the Pyramid of the Moon, walk the Avenue of the Dead, and visit the Temple of Quetzalcóatl. Opt for an early start to avoid crowds and enjoy the site in the golden morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Centro Histórico and visit the Museo Nacional de Antropología (if time permits en route back) or stop at a local artisan workshop near the hotel for a private hands-on experience in traditional Mexican crafts such as talavera painting or amate paper art. Alternatively, enjoy a leisurely exploration of the Barrio Chino (Chinatown) and the surrounding streets of the historic center.
day_by_day.evening: Pre-dinner mezcal tasting experience at a curated mezcalería such as La Clandestina or In Situ Mezcalería — sample rare single-origin mezcals from Oaxaca, Guerrero, and Durango with expert guidance on terroir and production methods. Dinner at Quintonil, another globally acclaimed restaurant by Chef Jorge Vallejo, celebrating native Mexican ingredients through a sophisticated tasting menu.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the hotel — granola with local honey, yogurt, fresh papaya, and strong café de olla before departure to Teotihuacán
meals.lunch: Private picnic lunch prepared by the hotel or a gourmet box from a local deli, enjoyed at the archaeological site with views of the pyramids — or lunch at La Gruta, a unique restaurant set inside a natural cave near Teotihuacán
meals.dinner: Quintonil — seasonal tasting menu featuring dishes such as nopales (cactus) ceviche, black bean tostadas with huitlacoche, and slow-cooked lamb barbacoa; natural wine and agave spirit pairing recommended

day_by_day.notes: Depart for Teotihuacán by 7:30–8:00 AM for the best experience. Wear sunscreen and a hat — the site is fully exposed. The hotel concierge can arrange a premium private vehicle and expert guide. La Gruta restaurant requires a reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private cooking class with a renowned local chef, hosted in a traditional Mexican kitchen near Centro Histórico. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as mole rojo, tamales, and agua de jamaica from scratch using ingredients sourced from a morning visit to the historic Mercado de Jamaica or Mercado de la Merced. This hands-on experience offers deep insight into Mexican culinary heritage and techniques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the stunning Museo del Palacio de Bellas Artes (Palace of Fine Arts), a masterpiece of Art Nouveau and Art Deco architecture housing extraordinary murals by Rivera, Orozco, Siqueiros, and Tamayo. Browse the museum's galleries and enjoy the extraordinary architecture inside and out. Afterward, explore the nearby Alameda Central park for a peaceful afternoon stroll and people-watching.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a live performance of Ballet Folklórico de México at the Palacio de Bellas Artes — a world-famous spectacle of traditional Mexican dance and music representing the country's diverse regional cultures, performed in one of the most beautiful theaters in the Americas. Pre-show dinner at a nearby premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — huevos rancheros with handmade tortillas, refried black beans, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and café de olla
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class — a multi-course meal prepared by you and your chef instructor, paired with artisanal mezcal or agua fresca in a traditional setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Limosneros — a sophisticated restaurant in a 17th-century colonial building near Bellas Artes, specializing in pre-Hispanic ingredients reimagined in contemporary Mexican cuisine; try the huitlacoche quesadillas and the duck in mole amarillo

day_by_day.notes: Ballet Folklórico performances typically take place on Wednesdays and Sundays — verify the schedule and book tickets in advance through the hotel concierge. The cooking class should be booked ahead of the trip. Mercado de Jamaica is a sensory highlight and ideal for early morning visits.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning — sleep in or enjoy a spa treatment at the hotel or a nearby luxury spa. For culture enthusiasts, visit the Museo José Luis Cuevas, a beautiful colonial building turned contemporary art museum just steps from the Zócalo, housing an impressive collection of modern Mexican and international art including a monumental bronze sculpture by Cuevas in the central courtyard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final luxury shopping experience on and around Madero Street and the surrounding historic streets — pick up premium artisan chocolates from MUCHO (Museo del Chocolate), high-end Mexican vanilla, specialty coffee, fine silver jewelry, or handcrafted leather goods as souvenirs. Enjoy a final walk through the Zócalo and take in the grandeur of the historic center one last time.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Contramar (if departing late) or a rooftop dining experience at one of Centro Histórico's premium hotel restaurants with panoramic views of the illuminated Zócalo and Metropolitan Cathedral — a truly unforgettable final evening in Mexico City. Enjoy a last mezcal cocktail as a toast to an extraordinary journey.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious final hotel breakfast — a full spread including freshly made tamales, enfrijoladas, tropical fruit, artisanal pastries, and specialty single-origin Mexican coffee
meals.lunch: El Cardenal (Palacio de Hierro branch or Tacuba location) — an institution for traditional Mexican cuisine, perfect for a refined final lunch; try the caldo tlalpeño, chiles en nogada, and arroz con leche
meals.dinner: Rooftop dinner at Hotel Downtown Mexico or a comparable luxury rooftop venue in Centro Histórico — contemporary Mexican cuisine with sweeping views of the illuminated historic skyline; signature cocktails with mezcal, tequila, and fresh tropical fruits

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private luxury transfer back to the airport well in advance — allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure given Mexico City traffic. Ask the hotel concierge to prepare a gourmet travel snack box for the journey. Consider purchasing a curated mezcal or artisanal gift set from the hotel boutique as a final memento.
